ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on two sides of $\triangle MON$, segments $OA$ and $OB$ are intercepted such that $OA = OB$; arcs are drawn with points A and B as centers and the length of $OA$ as the radius, intersecting at point C; segments $AC$, $BC$, $AB$, and $OC$ are connected. If $AB = 2\,\text{cm}$, and the area of quadrilateral $OACB$ is $4\,\text{cm}^{2}$, what is the length of $OC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: According to the drawing method, we have $AC=BC=OA$,\\
$\because$ $OA=OB$,\\
$\therefore$ $OA=OB=BC=AC$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $OACB$ is a rhombus.\\
$\because$ $AB=2\text{cm}$, and the area of quadrilateral $OACB$ is $4\text{cm}^2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}AB\times OC=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times OC=4$,\\
Solving yields $OC=\boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, triangle MON can be seen, point O is at the lower left, point M is above, and point N is at the lower right; point A is located on side OM, and point B is located on side ON. In the figure, OA, OB, AB, AC, BC, and OC are connected, forming quadrilateral O-A-C-B, in which AB and OC are the two diagonals of this quadrilateral. Then reason: By the construction in the problem, OA=OB. Draw an arc with A as the center and OA as the radius, and it passes through intersection point C, so AC=OA; draw an arc with B as the center and OA as the radius, and it passes through intersection point C, so BC=OA. Therefore OA=OB=BC=AC, the four sides of quadrilateral OACB are equal, and it is a rhombus. The area of a rhombus is equal to one half of the product of its two diagonals, so S=(1/2)·AB·OC. It is known that AB=2 cm and the area is 4 cm²; substituting gives 4=(1/2)×2×OC=OC, therefore OC=4 cm.
